title: Build this workbench drafting table for under $50
summary: A dual-purpose workbench and drafting table, listed in the March 1979 Popular Mechanics contents. The title indicates a low-cost convertible workspace; the actual mechanism, bill of materials, construction sequence and historical price basis have not been independently inspected.
improve: Engineer a positive-locking tilt mechanism with mechanical stops and a secondary retaining pin, so the drafting surface cannot drop unexpectedly.
Set working height using an adjustable support range determined from the intended user's seated and standing elbow heights; reduces sustained shoulder and wrist strain.
Use stable, low-emission plywood with sealed edges and a replaceable hardboard or drafting-mat wear surface; improves flatness and serviceability.
Create a parametric CAD cut list and CNC/router drilling template for pivot locations, then test full-range interference before cutting; reduces fit-up errors and rework.
Add restrained cable routing, a removable pencil tray and anti-slip feet; prevents snagging, improves access and limits unintended movement.
